page: Amazon Web Services r7i.4xlarge is a memory-optimized server instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with an Intel Xeon 8488C processor operating at 3.2 GHz. The instance provides 16 virtual CPUs across 8 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, backed by a 105 MB L3 cache. It is equipped with 128.0 GB of high-speed 5 GHz DDR5 memory, yielding an 8.0 GB memory-to-core ratio. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPUs, and it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 6 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-threaded capabilities, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2141.0 and a strong single-threaded gzip compression rate of 33.78 GB/sec. The processor supports advanced instruction sets including Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and AVX-512, which assist in cryptographic and vector operations. Memory bandwidth tests show a read-only small block cached speed of 1379.96 GB/sec and a large block uncached write speed of 77.32 GB/sec. For specialized tasks, it achieves a strong text generation speed of 333.12 tokens/sec on small LLM models (135M), while multi-core operations like bzip3 decompression and software compilation perform in the average tier.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the r7i.4xlarge offers a dense DDR5 memory configuration relative to its vCPU count, making it a viable option for memory-bound workloads without the overhead of local storage. The absence of bundled local NVMe storage means storage requirements must be handled externally. This instance is well-suited for workloads such as in-memory databases, caching layers, data processing, and enterprise applications requiring high memory capacity and strong single-core performance.
